For President Trump, diesel is a political problem ahead of the Midterms because its role in farming states (and a slow moving economic challenge). But gasoline is, ultimately, a much larger issue, both politically and economically (look at gas / diesel weigh on CPI basket).

The good news for the White House is that gasoline prices are moving down (which explain some of the comments today by US Treasury Sec Bessent) 

As a rough rule of thumb, NY gasoline futures (in dollars per gallon) + ~$1 = nationwide average retail price. If so, US retail gasoline price heading to $4 a gallon if the trend in the wholesale market holds for several days. Wholesale prices fell today to a 2½-month low. Don't be surprised if Trump starts to complain loudly about Big Oil not moving quickly enough to lower pump prices.

Linked to the above, some data on the weighing of gasoline and diesel on US urban CPI calculations. Gasoline has a weigh of nearly 2.9% while diesel has a weighing of nearly 0.09% -- and that's not just diesel, but includes ethanol, and even electricity charging for EVs. https://t.co/spDVmpTIO0

MIDDLE EAST FLOWS: Not only flows have proven resilient, but over the last few days (particularly since Oct 16), SoH traffic has surged despite Iranian attacks.

Total Middle East crude flows (ex-Iran, including SoH and all the bypass pipelines and routes) are back to >90% of pre-war levels (last seen in late Sept), and even higher if using a short 7-day average. Refined products flows remain significantly below. Caveat: flows are very uneven, with some days of large number of tanker crossings, followed by very quiet days. 

Overall, physical Middle East crude oil premia has continued to drop; just the opposite of what has happened to flat prices. The Oman-Dubai differential has fallen to a 3-month low of ~$4 a barrel. The differential was >$30 a barrel in mid-Sept.

If you look at the BRENT oil chart, you will notice that the price began heading back up in early July, right before the brittle MoU effectively fell apart following a brief continuation in flows. To maintain flows, US CENTCOM stepped up efforts to shepherd tankers out of the SoH, and once that happened, everyone wanted to move more oil. It created a rat race for both oil and tankers.
A minority nonetheless; and most of these tankers that get hit, make it out to the GoO for an STS transfer.

The cited source (IMF Portwatch) only report what pings over AIS. Everyone and their brother knows by now that the overwhelming majority of tankers switch off their AIS transponders when traversing the Strait of Hormuz for security reasons.
